London, 30<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**GM CEO Rick Wagoner** has resigned under pressure from the Obama administration, to be replaced by COO Fritz Henderson. GM has 60 days to determine its future.  Chrysler will be given 30 days to complete a proposed alliance with Fiat SpA.; if successful, it could receive up to $6 billion in new assistance. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Toyota** led a 56 % decline in Japan’s domestic vehicle production last month, the biggest drop since at least 1967, on slumping U.S. and European demand.   Local production at Japan’s 12 automakers fell to 481,396 vehicles from a year earlier, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association said today. Exports dropped 64 % to 212,107 vehicles, with North American shipments falling 66 %. The output and export drops were the biggest since the group began tracking the data in 1973.  Toyota, Nissan, Mazda and Mitsubishi each cut domestic production by at least 60 % last month to trim inventory. Japan’s domestic auto production has posted record drops every month since November.   Toyota’s domestic production last month plunged 64 % to 141,127, the lowest level since the company began publishing tallies in 1976. Exports from Japan plunged 69 % to 72,595.  Honda’s production in Japan fell 48% to 54,748 vehicles, the biggest decline since it began releasing figures in August 1996. Nissan reported a 69 % fall in domestic production after exports slumped 78 %. Nissan is cutting output by 64,000 vehicles in Feb and Mar.  Mazda built 60 % fewer vehicles in Japan. Mitsubishi Motors cut domestic production by 77%. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Fuel-economy standards** for all U.S. light vehicles will rise 8 percent to an average of 27.3 mpg for the 2011 model year and will cost the industry $1.46 billion to change, the US government said today.  Cars will be required to travel an industry average of 30.2 miles on each gallon of fuel, up from 27.5 mpg, and light-truck standards will increase by 1 mpg, to 24.1 mpg. The combined fleet average will go up by 2 mpg. Car standards by company for 2011 will range from 27.5 mpg for Maserati and Tata Motors, which sells Jaguar, to 31.2 mpg for Porsche. On trucks, the lowest standard will be General Motors’ 23.3 mpg; the toughest: Mitsubishi’s 26.7 mpg.  The rules are the first fuel-economy mandates set by the Obama administration and will use a new system that sets standards for individual models based on their size. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**AU Optronics** will cancel its unpaid leave policy in April due to rising utilization, while CMO has significantly reduced the scope of such a measure.  They estimate utilization rates to reach full capacity in Q309 amid rising demand generated by China’s stimulus program. However, there have been no significant signs of recovery in demand from other regions. _Source: Digitimes_ 

**Eskom** might apply to the National Energy Regulator of South Africa for a 34% increase in

electricity tariffs for the coming year, much higher than the 20-25% price path outlined last year.  This is likely to trigger significant opposition from consumer and labour groupings.  The Congress of South African Trade Unions already indicated that it could take to the streets should Eskom request a substantial price hike. _Source:  Engineering Weekly_ 

**Aquarius Platinum** and its takeover target Ridge Mining on Friday announced that they had signed an implementation agreement, following which Aquarius would make an all-share offer for Ridge Mining. _Source: Mining Weekly_ 

**Braemore Resources** announced an operational incident at a furnace at Mintek’s ConRoast smelter. Initial investigations suggest superficial damage to the plant and minimal impact on production.The furnace is anticipated to return to full production within 10 days. _Source:  Braemore Resources_
